text: to start. Thank you may it please the court. Chapter 211 of the Texas local government code sets out procedures that are required whenever a city adopts a zoning ordinance and there are two distinct procedural paths. For initial zoning publication notice is required and there are no protest rights. For zoning changes regarding a specific property or a discrete area in property owners within 200 feet of the area being rezoned are entitled to individualized notice and protest rights that can trigger the requirement for a super majority vote if enough people protest and the dispute here is which procedural path applies to the city of Austin's comprehensive revision of its land development code. The trial court rendered judgment that the individualized notice and protest provisions apply. This court should reverse for three reasons. First the LDC revision considers the entire city all at once and it turns the zoning changes turn on broad policy determinations and decisions rather than property specific factors the way it would be if there were and just a one small property having a zoning changed and in that way the comprehensive revision of the LDC is like initial zoning and it is not like a zoning change regarding a specific piece of property. The procedures for initial zoning therefore should apply. Second the individualized notice and protest provisions make no sense at all when applied to a comprehensive revision of the land development code. The leading treatise on zoning under Texas law described that the individualized notice provisions are quote administratively difficult expensive and unnecessary where a well-publicized comprehensive revision like the city of Austin's are concerned and the protest provisions cannot be applied logically at all where the area being rezoned is the whole entire city but most important the only Texas case to have considered these issues the FLCT case held that the individualized notice provisions do not apply where an enactment that makes a zoning change that applies uniformly citywide and that precedent is helpful not just for the bottom line holding but also as a guide for how to analyze the issue.
